Inbound from Hacker News post -> signup. Small devtools startup building a code assistant IDE plugin. Interested in Hosted API (self-serve) first, may convert to Dedicated later if usage grows. Primary asks: long context support (multi-file PRs + repo history), predictable token rate limits, streaming SDKs for incremental code completions, and minimal cold-start latency for interactive flows.

Call summary (3/5) w/ Maya + Jamal:
- Found via blog post about large context windows. Said: "We have 100k token conversation slices for PR+CI context; need a reliable way to pass large histories without excessive cost."
- Wants per-route rate limits (team-level quota) and ability to throttle per-user keys. Concerned about noisy CI traffic.
- Asked about SDKs: node/python preferred, web/wasm for plugin. Wants streaming websocket + server-side SDK.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB — wants clear guardrails to avoid runaway spend. Looking for batching/caching recommendations.
- Security: SSO for internal team, KMS for secrets at rest, audit logs for compliance (no enterprise EHR-level requirements yet).

POC plan:
- They will onboard test org this week (used free credits from signup). Running two scenarios: 1) interactive plugin completions with 4 developers concurrently; 2) nightly repo indexing and embedding updates (~10k files).
- Milestone 1 (3/18): validate streaming latency <200ms per token for interactive paths (50 concurrent streams).
- Milestone 2 (3/25): evaluate cost per 10k tokens with caching + batching enabled; ask Redwood Optimize suggestions.

Internal notes / AE playbook:

- Provide clear rate-limit tiers and per-route limit examples (e.g., 50 rps/team, 5 rps/user) and sample guardrail config in Console.
- Put them in trial org with elevated trial quotas for 2 weeks; connect to Jamal for deep-dive on throughput tuning.
- Legal: will request standard DPA + SOC2 checklist; hand to solutions engineer early.
